chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Sinan from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan said:
I was informed about Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he disliked the purchase of what has not been seen.

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir), a key Shia Imam
key_terms.مَا لَمْ يُرَ: What has not been seen (a specific type of sale involving unseen goods)
key_terms.يَكْرَهُ: He disliked (indicating a legal preference or ruling)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on selling goods that the buyer has not seen?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* attributes the dislike (*karahah*) of selling unseen goods (*bay' al-ma'lum* or *bay' al-gharar*) to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), reflecting the Shia emphasis on transparency to prevent dispute. It underscores the practical application of avoiding *gharar* (ambiguity) in commercial contracts, a principle widely discussed by later jurists like Al-Sharif al-Murtada and Al-Majlisi in their commentaries on trade ethics.
